summary: Owned Chinese in s0421–s0629 supplies only a handful of era clauses—咸和初, 建興中, 太興二年, 咸和八年, 九年, 建興二十一年, 永和元年, 永和二年—plus 在位二十二年卒時年四十, 父卒時年十六, and 卒時年二十七. Almost every owned claim still writes a closed Western year from an external Jin table (Xianhe 5, Xiankang 1/4, Yonghe 3/5/6/8/9, and ancient BC/AD life years). Those endpoints date uncertainty as if it were a known event year, or treat a whole reign as one activity window. Speeches that say 昔西門豹 / 光武 / 樂毅 / 漢高 are later reception, not living chronology; 勒雄既死 and 懷恨九泉 / 穆帝追諡 are retrospective or posthumous and must not feed life dates or active hints. Zhang Jun and Zhang Chonghua are missing death and age claims; Yonghe 9 as Chonghua’s end contradicts 時年二十七 and 在位十一年. A few items are supported: Wang Feng’s thanks-mission after 咸和八年 (AD 333 as a year-label), Ma Ji under 永和元年 (AD 345), the two mothers’ Yonghe-2 honors (AD 346), and undated Yuan Meng. Wang Feng’s hint still fails because 九年復使訪隨豐等 is omitted. Calendar checks confirm the era-label arithmetic where the Chinese actually names the year; they do not authorize inventing years the text never wrote.
